transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, um, my manager actually told me I needed to come in. I'm a waitress, and I've been at the same restaurant for a while now, and usually I'm really good at handling the dinner rush, you know? I even went to college for a couple of years before I started serving, so I know how to organize my thoughts and multitask. But lately... well, what really scared everyone at work—the other girls on shift, my manager, everybody—is that I just started freezing up right in the middle of service. 

Like, completely freezing. Or I'll start doing things completely out of order, which makes no sense because I know the routine backwards and forwards. Like, the other day, it was the middle of the lunch rush, and I was supposed to be closing out checks for my section. But instead of doing that, they found me just... standing over by the soda station. I was just standing there holding the cash drawer key in my hand, just gripping it, and I was just repeating table numbers out loud. Like, "table four, table nine, table twelve," just saying them over and over instead of actually closing the checks. I don't even really know how long I was standing there doing it, but my manager pulled me aside and said it really freaked people out and that I needed to get checked out before I could come back to work. Because you just can't do that when you have a section full of hungry people waiting on you, you know? So I guess that's why I'm here, to figure out why I'm getting stuck like that.
Have you ever felt like you're seeing, hearing, or believing things that other people don't seem to notice or understand?

Well, um, it's funny you ask that, because... well, yes. But it's not like I'm seeing ghosts or anything like that. It's more like... okay, so you know how when you're closing down the restaurant, it gets really quiet? Like, all the background noise from the customers and the clinking plates and the kitchen yelling, it all just stops. And it's just you and maybe one other closer and the manager in the back office. Well, sometimes when I'm doing my checkout, counting my tips and my bank, I'll hear this voice. 

It's a woman's voice, and it sounds so real, like she's standing right over my shoulder. Sometimes she just says my name, like, "Hey," or just my name, you know? But other times, it's when I'm doing the math for my checkout. I'll be counting the cash, separating the ones and the fives and the twenties, trying to make sure my drawer balances, and she'll just say, clear as day, "You're doing the count wrong." And the first few times it happened, I actually turned around and answered her! I was like, "No, I'm not, I've got it right here," and I looked behind me, and there was nobody there. The other closer was all the way across the dining room rolling silverware. 

And it's not just at work, either. It happens when I'm at home, too, usually when I'm in my own kitchen. I'll be making a sandwich or pouring a glass of water, and I'll hear her again. Just my name, or a comment about what I'm doing. And I always answer back before my brain catches up and realizes that I live alone and there's absolutely no one else in the apartment. It's so strange because it doesn't sound like a thought in my head, you know? It sounds like it's coming from outside of me, from the room. And I haven't told anyone at work about it because, I mean, after the whole freezing up thing, I don't want them to think I'm completely losing it. But it happens enough that I've started second-guessing myself when I'm doing my checkout, wondering if maybe I really am doing the count wrong, even though I know I'm good at math. I mean, I took college algebra, I know how to count a cash drawer. But when you hear someone tell you you're wrong that clearly, it really messes with your head.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that you know are completely true, but you realize most other people would say they aren't real or don't make sense?

Well, it's... I mean, yes. I have this situation going on right now, actually, and it's driving me absolutely crazy because nobody believes me, not even my own husband. See, at the restaurant, there are these two other servers—they usually work the patio section, which is highly coveted, by the way, because that's where the big tops sit and the tips are better—and I know for an absolute fact that they are trying to get me fired. And it's not just them, they've somehow gotten one of our regular customers involved, this guy who comes in every Tuesday and Thursday for the early dinner rush. 

I know it sounds crazy to other people, but I can literally feel them watching me whenever I'm at the POS system. You know, the computer terminal where we punch in the orders? I'll be standing there, trying to type in a complicated order with a bunch of modifications, and I can feel their eyes just burning into the back of my neck, watching exactly how I ring things in. And the proof is on the tickets. The kitchen prints out these duplicate order tickets, and I started noticing these little signs on them. Like, there will be an extra space before the word "ranch," or the time stamp will be exactly one minute off from the clock on the wall, or a modification will be typed in all lowercase when the system defaults to uppercase. It's this whole subtle code they're using, leaving these little markers on the tickets to build this huge case against me, to make it look like I'm incompetent and messing up the inventory so the manager has an excuse to let me go. 

I even started bringing some of the duplicate receipts home in my apron to prove it. I laid them all out on the kitchen table for my husband last week. I was pointing right at the weird spacing and the lowercase letters, showing him exactly how it all connects back to those two servers and that regular customer, but he just looked at me like I was speaking another language. He told me I was overthinking it and said it’s just normal restaurant mess-ups, like somebody's thumb slipped on the screen or the old receipt printer in the kitchen is just glitching again. But you don't just glitch the exact same way three shifts in a row! I know what I'm seeing, and I know they're plotting against me, but because nobody else will actually look at the evidence, they all just think I'm making it up or being paranoid. But I'm not. It's really happening right in front of them.
Have you had these beliefs about people trying to get you fired and the signs on the order tickets for at least six months now?

Six months? Um, no, it hasn't been quite that long. Let me think about it, because, you know, in the restaurant industry, time just kind of blurs together. You're just living shift to shift, lunch rush to dinner rush, and sometimes you don't even know what day of the week it is unless you look at the specials board. 

But if I really sit down and trace it back... the really clear stuff, like hearing that woman's voice so plainly when I'm doing my bank at night, and having those firm, undeniable beliefs about the patio servers and that regular customer targeting me... that really all solidified about four months ago. Yeah, it would be about four months. Because I remember it was right around the time we did the big seasonal menu rollout, which is always a complete nightmare anyway because they update the POS system and everyone is trying to memorize the new sides and modifiers. That's when I really started catching on to what they were doing with the tickets and the spacing. 

Before that, I mean, I was stressed out, sure, but the actual clearer voices and the absolute certainty that they are coordinating this whole thing to get me fired? That's been going on for a solid four months now. And let me tell you, four months feels like an absolute eternity when you have to go into work every single day on high alert. I spend my whole shift just watching my back, checking every single duplicate receipt that prints out of the kitchen, making sure my cash drawer is absolutely perfect so they can't use it against me, and it's just exhausting. Four months of that kind of stress will really wear a person down, you know? Because you can't just clock out and leave it behind when you know they're probably texting each other about you the second you walk out the door.
Have you experienced any signs or symptoms like these—such as hearing voices or feeling like people are plotting against you—for at least six months now?

Well, if you mean just the start of it all... like, any signs that something was off or that things were starting to shift, then yes, definitely longer than six months. Like I said before, the really intense stuff, the clear voice and catching them using the ticket codes, that was four months ago. But if I really think about it, this whole change in me has been building for about a year and two months. 

It started exactly a year and two months ago, because that is when the general manager pulled me aside before a busy Friday night and asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities. Which, I mean, it sounds like a good thing, like a promotion, right? But in the restaurant industry, being a shift lead just means you do all the manager work for barely any extra hourly pay. You have to handle the voids, the comps, deal with angry tables when the kitchen overcooks a steak, and you have to make sure every single server rolls their silverware and does their sidework before they are allowed to get cut and go home. 

And that is when everything really started shifting. I remember feeling this massive change in the atmosphere almost immediately. I would walk into the waitstation to grab a stack of napkins or restock the straws, and it felt like everyone had just stopped whispering about me the second the door swung open. I started feeling this heavy pressure, like all eyes were on me, just waiting for me to fail at being the lead. I was so stressed out about balancing the master drawer and dealing with the nightly deposits that I just felt my whole personality changing. I was on edge all the time, always looking over my shoulder, always wondering what those patio servers were saying behind my back because they were mad they did not get the lead position. 

So the really loud, undeniable stuff with the receipts and the voice telling me my math is wrong, that is more recent. But the actual beginning of this whole change, this feeling that things were wrong and people were against me? That has been building up for a year and two months, ever since I got those shift lead keys. It is just that nobody warns you how much a tiny bit of authority is going to completely ruin your life and make everyone turn on you, and it just slowly built up and built up until we got to where we are now.

Are these experiences—like hearing the voice or feeling like people are plotting against you—something you notice all the time, even when you're not at work or doing tasks like counting your cash drawer?

Well, it’s... it’s not every single second of the day, but it definitely follows me home. It’s not just when I’m at the restaurant or staring at the POS system. Like, you asked if it happens outside of work, and it absolutely does. 

Sometimes it happens during closing, when I’m in the back office with that awful flickering fluorescent light that always gives me a migraine, just trying to finish up the deposit so I can finally leave. But then other times, I’ll literally just be at home, in my own kitchen. I’ll just be standing there, maybe making a cup of chamomile tea to try and unwind after a brutal ten-hour shift on my feet, or just organizing the mail on the counter because my husband just lets it pile up for days if I don't deal with it, and out of nowhere, I hear her. 

It’s a woman’s voice. And it is so, so incredibly clear. She’ll just say my name, right out loud, or she’ll tell me I’m doing the count wrong. Which is so strange because half the time at home I’m not even counting anything, I'm just trying to relax, but she says it anyway. And it sounds so real, so much like a physical person standing directly behind my left shoulder, that I actually answer her out loud. I’ll turn around and say, "What do you want?" or "No, I'm doing it right," and then... I just freeze. Because I’ll realize the house is completely quiet, my husband is in the other room watching TV, and there is absolutely nobody else in the kitchen with me. 

I'll just be standing there holding a mug or a stack of envelopes, realizing nobody else heard it. But I mean, how can nobody else hear it when it’s loud enough for me to reflexively answer back? It just makes my heart pound out of my chest. It’s exhausting enough trying to keep track of the patio servers and the duplicate tickets at work, but to come home and have this woman's voice telling me I'm messing up my count while I'm standing in my own kitchen... it just never really stops, you know? You never really get to just turn your brain off and rest.

Can you think back and tell me if there was ever a time when you experienced these kinds of things—like hearing the voice or believing others were plotting against you—for at least one month straight without a break?

Well, if you mean for a solid month without a single break... yeah, absolutely. Like I was saying earlier, the really intense part of all this, the clear voice and the absolute certainty that the patio servers and that regular customer are plotting against me with the tickets... that's been happening for about four months straight. 

And when I say four months straight, I mean it hasn't stopped for a single day. Not one day. Even on my days off, which, let's be honest, in the restaurant business a day off isn't really a day off. You're just recovering from the last shift and dreading the next one. You're doing laundry, trying to get the smell of fry oil out of your non-slip shoes, and the whole time, my mind is just racing. I'll be sitting on my couch, trying to watch a show, and I'm just replaying every single interaction I had with the patio servers the night before. Did they look at me weird when I ran their food? Why did they group their tickets like that? 

And the voice... she doesn't take a day off either. Like I told you, she's there when I'm just trying to make tea in my own kitchen. So, yes, to answer your question, it has definitely been at least a month straight. It's been four months of this constant, exhausting cycle. Four months of feeling like I have to be a detective in my own workplace, analyzing every receipt, every glance, every whisper in the waitstation. You just get so tired, doctor. You get so tired of always being on high alert, always waiting for the other shoe to drop, always waiting for them to finally make their move and get me fired. It's been four months of this, every single day, and I just... I don't know how much longer I can keep this up before I just completely break down in the middle of a dinner rush.
Would you say that your symptoms—like hearing the voice and believing others are plotting against you—have been present for at least six months now without a significant break?

Well, wait, no... I think maybe we are getting the timelines a little crossed here. Like I was just trying to explain a minute ago, the really clear voices? The woman's voice telling me my count is wrong in the kitchen, and that absolute, firm belief that the patio servers and that one regular customer are specifically targeting me with the ticket codes? That specific stuff has only been happening for about four months. 

It hasn't been six months for the voice and the plotting. Six months ago, I was just incredibly stressed out. I was feeling that heavy pressure, you know, feeling like everyone was whispering about me and watching me fail at being the shift lead, but I wasn't actually hearing her voice out loud yet. I wasn't catching them manipulating the receipts yet. All of that really intense, undeniable stuff started exactly four months ago. 

I remember clearly because it was right when corporate made us roll out the new spring menu, and I was already pulling my hair out trying to memorize all the new allergy modifiers for the seasonal salads so I could test the servers on them during pre-shift meetings. And that is exactly when the voice started chiming in and I finally realized what they were actually doing with the duplicate tickets. So, the firm beliefs and the clearer voices, that is a solid four months. The overall feeling of things being wrong and the atmosphere shifting, that is the year and two months. I just want to make sure I'm being completely accurate with you, because I know six months is what you keep asking about, but the really loud, constant stuff where I'm catching them plotting is definitely just a four-month thing.

Would you say that your experiences—like hearing the woman’s voice and believing the others are plotting against you—have been happening almost every day for at least six months straight, without a significant break?

I feel like we might be going in circles a bit here, doctor, because I know you keep asking about that six-month mark, but like I was just trying to explain... no. It hasn't been six months for those specific things. 

I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, so I have to be clear that the clearer voices—like that woman telling me I'm messing up my count—and those really firm beliefs I have about my coworkers and that regular customer targeting me... that has only been happening for about four months. 

I mean, if we go back six months ago, sure, I was an absolute wreck. I was working these awful back-to-back doubles, my feet were just throbbing by the end of the night, and I had this terrible, heavy feeling that people were whispering about me or waiting for me to mess up my shift lead duties. But I wasn't actually hearing her speak to me out loud yet, and I hadn't figured out the whole plot with the duplicate tickets yet. All of that really undeniable, intense stuff where I finally realized exactly what they were doing to me? That started exactly four months ago. 

I know it was four months because, like I said, it was right when corporate shoved that spring menu down our throats. I remember standing at the main POS terminal, just staring at this ticket that made absolutely no sense, completely overwhelmed by all the new allergy modifiers, and that is the exact moment the puzzle pieces clicked together about the patio servers. And it's the exact same time her voice started chiming in, clear as a bell, telling me I was doing it all wrong. So, no, not six months. It’s been exactly four months of the voices and the plotting happening every single day without a break. Four very long, very exhausting months, but definitely only four.

Have your experiences with hearing the woman’s voice and believing your coworkers are plotting against you occurred nearly every day and continued without a significant break for at least six months total?

Doctor, I... I really don't mean to be difficult, I promise I don't, but I feel like you're not hearing me on the timeline here. You keep asking me about this six-month mark, over and over, and I keep trying to explain that the math just doesn't add up that way. 

The really clear stuff—the woman's voice, the absolute, undeniable proof that the patio servers and that regular are plotting against me with the tickets—that has only been happening for about four months. Four months. 

I mean, if we're talking about six months ago, I was just a stressed-out mess. I was exhausted, pulling doubles, my feet were killing me, and I had this awful, sinking feeling that everyone was waiting for me to fail as a shift lead. I felt the pressure, I felt the eyes on me, sure. But I wasn't hearing her voice out loud yet. I hadn't connected the dots on the duplicate tickets yet. 

All of that—the voice telling me my count is wrong, the realization of what they're doing to get me fired—that started exactly four months ago. I know this for a fact because, like I said, it was right during the spring menu rollout. I remember standing at the POS terminal, just completely overwhelmed by the new allergy modifiers for the salads, and that's when it all clicked. That's when I saw what they were doing with the tickets, and that's when her voice started chiming in, clear as day. 

So, no, it hasn't been six months of the voices and the plotting. It's been exactly four months. Four very long, very exhausting months of dealing with this every single day, but definitely only four. I just really need you to understand that, because I feel like we keep circling back to six months, and that's just not when the really intense stuff started.
Have your experiences with hearing the woman’s voice and believing your coworkers are plotting against you occurred at all over the past six months, even if not every single day?

Well, I mean, if you're asking if it happened *at all* during the last six months, then I guess technically, yes, because four months is inside of six months, right? But I just... I really, really need to be clear here, because I feel like the timeline is getting all smudged together. 

The really clear stuff? The woman's voice actually speaking to me, telling me I'm messing up the drawer count, and that absolute, rock-solid realization that the patio servers and that one regular customer are actively targeting me with those ticket codes? That has only been happening for about four months. 

I know I keep saying four months, but it's just so vivid in my mind. It was that spring menu rollout. I can still picture the exact POS screen, the way the glare from the overhead lights hit it, and I was staring at this ticket that had, like, three different allergy modifiers on a seasonal salad, which we were supposed to memorize for the pre-shift, and my brain was just spinning. And right then, right in that exact moment, the voice chimed in. Just... clear as a bell. And I finally saw what they were doing with the duplicate tickets. It was like a veil was lifted. 

So, yes, it has happened *within* the last six months, but only for the last four of them. Before that four-month mark, like I was trying to explain, I was just incredibly stressed. I was working those awful back-to-back doubles, my feet were just absolute agony by the end of the night, and I had this terrible, heavy, crushing feeling that people were whispering about me or waiting for me to fail as a shift lead. I felt the pressure, I felt the eyes on me... but I wasn't hearing her voice out loud yet. I hadn't connected the dots on the plot yet. That intense, undeniable stuff where I'm catching them plotting and hearing her critique my counts, that is exactly a four-month thing. Not six. Just four very long, very exhausting months.
Would you say that, over the past six months, you have had any days where you experienced the voice or the belief that others were plotting against you, even if not every day?

Doctor, I... I feel like I'm just repeating myself, and I really don't want to be frustrating for you to deal with, but I just don't understand why we keep getting stuck on this six-month wording. Are you asking if I had, like, random days six months ago where I heard her, or sporadic days where I thought they were plotting? Because if that's what you mean, then the answer is definitely no. 

Like I've been trying to explain, the clearer voices and those really firm beliefs about my coworkers and that regular customer targeting me... that has been happening for about four months. Exactly four months. 

Before that, like five or six months ago, there weren't *any* days where I heard her voice. Not a single one. I was just a normal, exhausted shift lead working way too many back-to-back doubles, dealing with swollen feet—I actually had to buy completely new non-slip shoes because my feet were aching so badly—and just feeling this heavy anxiety that everyone was judging my closing duties. I felt the pressure, sure, but I wasn't hearing anyone actually speak to me out loud. 

It wasn't until that spring menu rollout four months ago that the actual plot started. And once it started, it wasn't just "some days"—it was every single day. So yes, technically it happened *during* the last six months, because four months is inside of six months, but the actual, real stuff? The clear voice telling me my drawer count is wrong and the absolute proof of the patio servers targeting me? That is strictly a four-month thing. I just really need to make sure you're writing down four months, because I want to be perfectly accurate, and six months just isn't the right timeline for when this actually began.
Would you say that, over the past six months, you have had any days where you experienced the voice or the belief that others were plotting against you, even if not every day?

I'm sorry, I... wait, didn't you literally just ask me that? I feel like we are just completely going in circles here, or maybe I'm just not explaining myself right, but I am trying so, so hard to make you understand the timeline. I know you have your checklist and your specific questions you have to get through, but it feels like you're not actually listening to what I'm saying. 

Like I just said a second ago, the clearer voices—her voice telling me I'm messing up—and those firm beliefs about my coworkers and that regular customer targeting me... that has been happening for about four months. Four months. Not six. 

I don't know how else to explain it so that it makes sense for your notes. Four months ago, we did the spring menu rollout. I remember it so vividly because management made us come in early for this whole hour-long tasting pre-shift, and I was already just completely drained from closing the night before, and my heels were absolutely throbbing in those new non-slip shoes I was telling you about. And that was the exact day it all shifted. That was the day the voice actually started speaking to me, clear as day, and I finally realized what the patio servers were doing with the tickets to sabotage my drawer counts. 

Before that specific day, like five or six months ago? There was nothing like that. No voices. No grand plot. Just me being a stressed-out shift lead trying to keep my head above water. So, yes, if you look at a calendar, I have experienced these things during the last six months, because the last four months are *inside* of that six-month window. And once it started four months ago, it hasn't been just "some days"—it's been every single day. I just really, really need you to write down that it's been exactly four months, because asking me about six months over and over makes me feel like you're trying to put words in my mouth, and I want to be perfectly accurate about when they actually started coming after me.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt down, depressed, or hopeless nearly every day, or lost interest in most activities you used to enjoy?

I mean... I don't know if "depressed" is the exact word I would use, because it's not like I'm sitting around crying all day, you know? But as far as losing interest in things... yeah. Yeah, absolutely. It's actually been really hard. 

I used to do so much before all this pressure at the restaurant started weighing on me. Like, I used to absolutely love going for beach walks. We don't live right on the water, but it’s just a short drive, and I used to go down there and just walk for miles, looking at the shells and the tide pools, just letting the breeze clear my head. I haven't done that in... I don't even know how long. And baking! I used to bake all the time. Sourdough, blueberry muffins, banana bread—my kitchen used to always smell like yeast and vanilla. Now my expensive stand mixer just sits on the counter collecting dust. 

I don't even garden anymore, either. I had this whole little setup in the backyard, and my tomato plants completely shriveled up and died this summer because I just stopped watering them. I couldn't even bring myself to go out there with the hose for five minutes. I even stopped writing in my journal, which I used to do every single morning with my coffee before my shifts. I had these specific fine-tip pens I liked to use, and I’d write down my thoughts or my goals for the day, but that notebook is just sitting on my nightstand, totally blank. 

And it's not just the hobbies. It's... it's with people, too. My husband, he tries so hard, he really does. He'll sit down next to me on the couch when I finally get home, and he tries to talk with me about his day, or ask what we should do on my day off, or just try to have a normal conversation. And I mostly just sit there. I just stare. It's not that I'm trying to be mean to him or shut him out, it's just... it feels like I can’t get myself to care. About any of it. I can't bring myself to start a conversation, or start an activity, or start anything at all. It's like the starter motor in my brain is just completely broken and everything is just too much effort. So, yeah, I guess I really have lost interest in pretty much everything I used to enjoy.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt a loss of pleasure or interest in all, or almost all, activities you used to enjoy, nearly every day?

I... I'm sorry, but we're doing the repeating thing again. Are you just reading down a list of questions that sound exactly the same? Because I feel like I literally just answered this for you. 

Like I just finished saying two seconds ago, I don't really go for beach walks, bake, garden, or write in my journal much anymore. At all, really. I gave up on all of it. And it's exactly like I was just explaining about my husband—when he tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there. I just sit on the couch while he's talking because it genuinely feels like I can't get myself to care or start anything. 

It's not just a passing phase or a couple of bad days, it is every single day. I just cannot bring myself to start a single thing, whether it's pulling weeds in the yard, or getting out my baking supplies, or even just having a basic conversation in my own living room with the man I married. The energy to care is just gone. So, yes, if you need me to confirm that specific wording for your checklist, then yes, I have lost pleasure and interest in all of it.

Well, um, my manager actually told me I needed to come in. I'm a waitress, and I've been at the same restaurant for a while now, and usually I'm really good at handling the dinner rush, you know? I even went to college for a couple of years before I started serving, so I know how to organize my thoughts and multitask. But lately... well, what really scared everyone at work—the other girls on shift, my manager, everybody—is that I just started freezing up right in the middle of service. 

Like, completely freezing. Or I'll start doing things completely out of order, which makes no sense because I know the routine backwards and forwards. Like, the other day, it was the middle of the lunch rush, and I was supposed to be closing out checks for my section. But instead of doing that, they found me just... standing over by the soda station. I was just standing there holding the cash drawer key in my hand, just gripping it, and I was just repeating table numbers out loud. Like, "table four, table nine, table twelve," just saying them over and over instead of actually closing the checks. I don't even really know how long I was standing there doing it, but my manager pulled me aside and said it really freaked people out and that I needed to get checked out before I could come back to work. Because you just can't do that when you have a section full of hungry people waiting on you, you know? So I guess that's why I'm here, to figure out why I'm getting stuck like that.

Well, um, it's funny you ask that, because... well, yes. But it's not like I'm seeing ghosts or anything like that. It's more like... okay, so you know how when you're closing down the restaurant, it gets really quiet? Like, all the background noise from the customers and the clinking plates and the kitchen yelling, it all just stops. And it's just you and maybe one other closer and the manager in the back office. Well, sometimes when I'm doing my checkout, counting my tips and my bank, I'll hear this voice. 

It's a woman's voice, and it sounds so real, like she's standing right over my shoulder. Sometimes she just says my name, like, "Hey," or just my name, you know? But other times, it's when I'm doing the math for my checkout. I'll be counting the cash, separating the ones and the fives and the twenties, trying to make sure my drawer balances, and she'll just say, clear as day, "You're doing the count wrong." And the first few times it happened, I actually turned around and answered her! I was like, "No, I'm not, I've got it right here," and I looked behind me, and there was nobody there. The other closer was all the way across the dining room rolling silverware. 

And it's not just at work, either. It happens when I'm at home, too, usually when I'm in my own kitchen. I'll be making a sandwich or pouring a glass of water, and I'll hear her again. Just my name, or a comment about what I'm doing. And I always answer back before my brain catches up and realizes that I live alone and there's absolutely no one else in the apartment. It's so strange because it doesn't sound like a thought in my head, you know? It sounds like it's coming from outside of me, from the room. And I haven't told anyone at work about it because, I mean, after the whole freezing up thing, I don't want them to think I'm completely losing it. But it happens enough that I've started second-guessing myself when I'm doing my checkout, wondering if maybe I really am doing the count wrong, even though I know I'm good at math. I mean, I took college algebra, I know how to count a cash drawer. But when you hear someone tell you you're wrong that clearly, it really messes with your head.

Well, it's... I mean, yes. I have this situation going on right now, actually, and it's driving me absolutely crazy because nobody believes me, not even my own husband. See, at the restaurant, there are these two other servers—they usually work the patio section, which is highly coveted, by the way, because that's where the big tops sit and the tips are better—and I know for an absolute fact that they are trying to get me fired. And it's not just them, they've somehow gotten one of our regular customers involved, this guy who comes in every Tuesday and Thursday for the early dinner rush. 

I know it sounds crazy to other people, but I can literally feel them watching me whenever I'm at the POS system. You know, the computer terminal where we punch in the orders? I'll be standing there, trying to type in a complicated order with a bunch of modifications, and I can feel their eyes just burning into the back of my neck, watching exactly how I ring things in. And the proof is on the tickets. The kitchen prints out these duplicate order tickets, and I started noticing these little signs on them. Like, there will be an extra space before the word "ranch," or the time stamp will be exactly one minute off from the clock on the wall, or a modification will be typed in all lowercase when the system defaults to uppercase. It's this whole subtle code they're using, leaving these little markers on the tickets to build this huge case against me, to make it look like I'm incompetent and messing up the inventory so the manager has an excuse to let me go. 

I even started bringing some of the duplicate receipts home in my apron to prove it. I laid them all out on the kitchen table for my husband last week. I was pointing right at the weird spacing and the lowercase letters, showing him exactly how it all connects back to those two servers and that regular customer, but he just looked at me like I was speaking another language. He told me I was overthinking it and said it’s just normal restaurant mess-ups, like somebody's thumb slipped on the screen or the old receipt printer in the kitchen is just glitching again. But you don't just glitch the exact same way three shifts in a row! I know what I'm seeing, and I know they're plotting against me, but because nobody else will actually look at the evidence, they all just think I'm making it up or being paranoid. But I'm not. It's really happening right in front of them.

patient.answer:
Doctor, I... I feel like I'm just repeating myself, and I really don't want to be frustrating for you to deal with, but I just don't understand why we keep getting stuck on this six-month wording. Are you asking if I had, like, random days six months ago where I heard her, or sporadic days where I thought they were plotting? Because if that's what you mean, then the answer is definitely no. 

Like I've been trying to explain, the clearer voices and those really firm beliefs about my coworkers and that regular customer targeting me... that has been happening for about four months. Exactly four months. 

Before that, like five or six months ago, there weren't *any* days where I heard her voice. Not a single one. I was just a normal, exhausted shift lead working way too many back-to-back doubles, dealing with swollen feet—I actually had to buy completely new non-slip shoes because my feet were aching so badly—and just feeling this heavy anxiety that everyone was judging my closing duties. I felt the pressure, sure, but I wasn't hearing anyone actually speak to me out loud. 

It wasn't until that spring menu rollout four months ago that the actual plot started. And once it started, it wasn't just "some days"—it was every single day. So yes, technically it happened *during* the last six months, because four months is inside of six months, but the actual, real stuff? The clear voice telling me my drawer count is wrong and the absolute proof of the patio servers targeting me? That is strictly a four-month thing. I just really need to make sure you're writing down four months, because I want to be perfectly accurate, and six months just isn't the right timeline for when this actually began.

patient.answer:
I'm sorry, I... wait, didn't you literally just ask me that? I feel like we are just completely going in circles here, or maybe I'm just not explaining myself right, but I am trying so, so hard to make you understand the timeline. I know you have your checklist and your specific questions you have to get through, but it feels like you're not actually listening to what I'm saying. 

Like I just said a second ago, the clearer voices—her voice telling me I'm messing up—and those firm beliefs about my coworkers and that regular customer targeting me... that has been happening for about four months. Four months. Not six. 

I don't know how else to explain it so that it makes sense for your notes. Four months ago, we did the spring menu rollout. I remember it so vividly because management made us come in early for this whole hour-long tasting pre-shift, and I was already just completely drained from closing the night before, and my heels were absolutely throbbing in those new non-slip shoes I was telling you about. And that was the exact day it all shifted. That was the day the voice actually started speaking to me, clear as day, and I finally realized what the patio servers were doing with the tickets to sabotage my drawer counts. 

Before that specific day, like five or six months ago? There was nothing like that. No voices. No grand plot. Just me being a stressed-out shift lead trying to keep my head above water. So, yes, if you look at a calendar, I have experienced these things during the last six months, because the last four months are *inside* of that six-month window. And once it started four months ago, it hasn't been just "some days"—it's been every single day. I just really, really need you to write down that it's been exactly four months, because asking me about six months over and over makes me feel like you're trying to put words in my mouth, and I want to be perfectly accurate about when they actually started coming after me.

patient.answer:
I mean... I don't know if "depressed" is the exact word I would use, because it's not like I'm sitting around crying all day, you know? But as far as losing interest in things... yeah. Yeah, absolutely. It's actually been really hard. 

I used to do so much before all this pressure at the restaurant started weighing on me. Like, I used to absolutely love going for beach walks. We don't live right on the water, but it’s just a short drive, and I used to go down there and just walk for miles, looking at the shells and the tide pools, just letting the breeze clear my head. I haven't done that in... I don't even know how long. And baking! I used to bake all the time. Sourdough, blueberry muffins, banana bread—my kitchen used to always smell like yeast and vanilla. Now my expensive stand mixer just sits on the counter collecting dust. 

I don't even garden anymore, either. I had this whole little setup in the backyard, and my tomato plants completely shriveled up and died this summer because I just stopped watering them. I couldn't even bring myself to go out there with the hose for five minutes. I even stopped writing in my journal, which I used to do every single morning with my coffee before my shifts. I had these specific fine-tip pens I liked to use, and I’d write down my thoughts or my goals for the day, but that notebook is just sitting on my nightstand, totally blank. 

And it's not just the hobbies. It's... it's with people, too. My husband, he tries so hard, he really does. He'll sit down next to me on the couch when I finally get home, and he tries to talk with me about his day, or ask what we should do on my day off, or just try to have a normal conversation. And I mostly just sit there. I just stare. It's not that I'm trying to be mean to him or shut him out, it's just... it feels like I can’t get myself to care. About any of it. I can't bring myself to start a conversation, or start an activity, or start anything at all. It's like the starter motor in my brain is just completely broken and everything is just too much effort. So, yeah, I guess I really have lost interest in pretty much everything I used to enjoy.

No new disorders were added or ruled out definitively at this time.

Like I just finished saying two seconds ago, I don't really go for beach walks, bake, garden, or write in my journal much anymore. At all, really. I gave up on all of it. It's not just a passing phase or a couple of bad days, it is every single day. I just cannot bring myself to start a single thing, whether it's pulling weeds in the yard, or getting out my baking supplies, or even just having a basic conversation in my own living room with the man I married. The energy to care is just gone. So, yes, if you need me to confirm that specific wording for your checklist, then yes, I have lost pleasure and interest in all of it.
